changelog.note: MASTER BOTTLE INTERFACE BREAK: p_bottle_d() 86 -> 84 mm (every other bottle dimension -- height, dome heights, cap/collar diameters, wall thickness -- held). Every value that cascades from bottle diameter moved accordingly: p_insert_shaft_d(), p_seal_groove_root_d(), p_port_height() / p_port_length() (== bottle diameter + taper/allowance terms), Ecojoiner john_height/john_length/rectangle_y, top_crossbar_len, bottom_rail_len, ballast core_w/slat_gap/slat_spacing/board_len/fin_len, rear-fin shaft_length, and the cage/cap/sail-frame radial-clearance chain (cage_notch_root_radius, bottom_sail_bar_inner_radius, etc.) that all key off the shared insert/cap-diameter derivation. build/build.py + build/lint.py run clean (0 problem groups). SHARED-CONTRACT CHANGE per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5: build/test.py and build/baseline.py were explicitly requested and run in this same pass, not just recommended. First full run: 7/30 passed, 23 bounds-moved failures -- all reviewed and confirmed as either (a) the intended bottle-diameter cascade above, (b) two items of PRE-EXISTING un-recorded drift unrelated to this change (control_cap's Z-max 40->68 from v2.2.0's side_tabs, never baselined; several wooden-part lengths that were still baselined against the even older 82 mm bottle from before the 86 mm change), or (c) one REAL BUG this run caught: src/components/Silicone_Ring_Mold.scad's flat_ring_inner_d/outer_d customizer literals (59.25/79.25) were hardcoded at build time for the 86 mm bottle in v2.3.1 and do not auto-track lib/params.scad -- corrected to 57.75/77.75 (matches p_seal_groove_root_d() x 0.75 stretch-fit + 10 mm radial width at 84 mm). No new ERROR or unexpected WARNING anywhere. Re-ran build/baseline.py (full set, all 30 renders) with review notes added to every changed tests/expected_bounds.json entry explaining its cause; deleted the orphaned hex_shaft__default entry (target renamed to sail_shaft in the TB-08 pass). Final confirmation run: build/test.py 30/30 renders passed clean against the new baseline. HopeTurtles.org generator propagation (CLAUDE.md s19) done in the same pass: fixed generator/sync_from_turtle_body.py (it was still looking for the pre-v1.7.1 'v1.0 SCADs/*_v1.scad' paths turtle_body renamed to 'scads_v1/*.scad' releases ago -- silently freezing the vendored snapshot at turtle_body ~1.8.3/bottle-82 this whole time), re-ran it, then generator/check_params_sync.py, which for the first time in a long while actually caught real drift (bottle_diameter 82 in the 6fc/fin/ballast/sails generator defaults, never actually updated for either the 86 or 84 mm bottle changes) -- fixed all four to 84; all 39 shared inputs now genuinely match. Also synced the sail-shaft (TB-08) design into generate_sails.py's embedded SCAD_TEMPLATE and objects/sails.py's 2D carpenter-sheet derivation (round shaft, Ø8.2 mm cage-hub/sail-bar hole, no hex, simplified joint strengthener) -- verified by generating and OpenSCAD-parsing all 8 sail-apparatus parts plus a rendered PDF carpenter sheet, no errors. See that repo's own SYNC_LOG.md entry for full detail.

TB-08: HARDWARE INTERFACE BREAK -- the centre axle drops its hex section entirely and becomes one uniform round Ø8 mm shaft, with a new lock mechanism. (1) Renamed lib/hex_shaft.scad's control_axle() to lib/sail_shaft.scad's sail_shaft() (wrapper Bottle_Hex_Shaft.scad -> Bottle_Sail_Shaft.scad, build/manifest.json id hex_shaft -> sail_shaft, stale stls_v1/Bottle_Hex_Shaft_v1.10.0.stl deleted -- no replacement STL exported in this pass, run build/export_stl.py when one is needed). The shaft is now a single cylinder(d=round_d, h=total_len) with the magnet recess at the lower end -- no join_overlap Boolean needed since there's only one piece. Total length held at 59 mm (p_axle_upper_len(), was p_axle_hex_len(), still 23 mm) so the existing cap/full-turtle placement transforms (control_assembly_z - (p_axle_upper_len()+p_axle_round_ext())) needed no change. (2) New p_axle_shaft_clearance() = 0.2 mm diametral running clearance and p_axle_shaft_hole_d() = p_axle_round_d() + that = 8.2 mm -- the ONE hole size now shared by both places the shaft passes through without bearing in: the cage hub bore (lib/control_cage.scad, was p_cage_hex_bore_af() = 10.3 mm hex AF, now a plain round cylinder) and the top sail bar's own hole (p_sail_bar_axle_hole_d(), was a hardcoded 12 mm sized for the ~11.55 mm hex-corner diameter). p_cap_axle_bore_d() (8.7, the cap's FREE-SPINNING bearing bore) is untouched -- it was already round and only ever sized for the shaft's uniform diameter, so the cap needed no change at all. (3) New shaft-to-cage lock: control_cage() gains a single radial M3 set screw through the hub wall (p_cage_setscrew_pilot_d() = 2.5 mm self-tapping pilot into the printed PLA hub -- untested thread engagement, not a clearance hole for a separate nut like the batten M3 holes; p_cage_setscrew_angle() = 0, adjustable) that presses directly on the shaft once it's inserted -- replaces the old hex-to-hex shape lock entirely. Modelled as a single cylinder drilled from the hub's outer surface in past the centre (cage_hub_bottom..cage_top Z-span asserted to contain it with margin), so it always reaches the shaft bore regardless of shaft_hole_d. (4) Cleaned up the inert cap/cage/axle parameter block duplicated in BOTH lib/sail_frame.scad and src/Full_Turtle.scad (kept only because their own asserts read from it, per CLAUDE.md s17): replaced every hex_shaft_across_flats/hex_corner_diameter/cage_centre_hex_* local + assert with round-shaft equivalents (cage_shaft_hole_diameter, shaft_upper_length), and DELETED three asserts in each file that had gone stale even before this change -- a 'central reinforcing wall' concept (cage_centre_hex_wall_height/thickness, cage_centre_hex_outer_corner_diameter) that does not exist in the actual lib/control_cage.scad module (which just cuts the bore straight through the solid hub) and duplicated/conflicted with the already-correct hub-fit check a few lines above it (cage_top_hole_radial_position - cage_top_hole_diameter/2 > cage_hub_diameter/2). Both files' remaining checks now literally mirror lib/control_cage.scad's own asserts. build/build.py + build/lint.py clean (0 problem groups) -- every assert in every render passed, including the two full asserts newly exercising the round-hole math. Rendered and inspected in OpenSCAD: Bottle_Sail_Shaft.scad (echo confirms 59/36/23 mm, Ø8 uniform, no hex); Bottle_Control_Cage.scad part=upright (echo confirms shaft hole 8.2, set-screw pilot 2.5 @ 0deg; --render gives Simple: yes, a single valid manifold solid); Full_Turtle_v1.scad assembly_view=top_sail and Turtle_Sail_Apparatus.scad part=assembly with show_control_bottle=true (no ERROR/WARNING, cap+cage+shaft+frame all sit together as expected). CLAUDE.md s3/s6/s9/s16/s19 updated for the rename and the new lock mechanism. HARDWARE INTERFACE BREAK per CLAUDE.md s15 step 6 rules (+1.0.0): an old printed hex shaft will not engage a new-design cage (no hex bore left to key into) and a new round shaft will not stay locked in an old-design cage (no set-screw hole to press against it) -- existing prints of either part do not interoperate with the other's new design. Per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5, this is a shared-contract change (lib/params.scad + two lib module signatures) -- build/test.py (full cross-subsystem mesh regression) and build/baseline.py (tests/expected_bounds.json is now stale for hex_shaft/control_cage/full_turtle/sail_apparatus -- the target itself was renamed hex_shaft->sail_shaft, so a maintainer baseline run is required, not optional, before this can be considered release-verified) were NOT run automatically -- recommended to the maintainer, not run. PLA-only + wooden sail-bar-hole change -- no HopeTurtles.org generator propagation needed (the generators' sails object never modelled an axle/hex hole at all; CLAUDE.md s19's PLA-only exemption covers the cap/cage/shaft side).

Simplified the joint strengthener per user feedback on the 2.3.2 redesign (screenshot showed both the new vertical screw hole and the leftover below-rail remnant as unwanted). Removed the vertical M6 screw clearance hole added in 2.3.2 -- not needed, the strengthener is held by the existing horizontal M6 bolt through the side batten alone. Removed the below-rail solid remnant + its now-pointless notch entirely: joint_strengthener_part() is now just the above-rail block (joint_strengthener_height = joint_strengthener_above_bar, was above_bar+bar_thickness+below_bar), its bottom face (Z=0) resting flush on the rail's own top surface. joint_strengthener_m6_z_local simplified to above_bar/2 (centred in the now-shorter block); joint_strengtheners_native_assembly()'s strengthener_z changed from bottom_bar_z-joint_strengthener_below_bar to bottom_bar_z+bottom_sail_bar_thickness (top of the rail) -- verified the M6 bolt's world Z is unchanged (side_batten_strengthener_m6_z_local already measured from the rail's top, so it needed no change). Removed the now-dead joint_strengthener_below_bar/slot_depth/slot_height locals and their two asserts. build/build.py + build/lint.py clean; rendered part=assembly (orthographic side-on and a close perspective) in OpenSCAD confirming the strengthener sits flush on the rail with no remnant below and no hole on top. Component-scoped to lib/sail_frame.scad, effect fully visible in the renders -- per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5, build/test.py was neither run nor recommended.

Fixed the show_control_bottle reference geometry added in 2.3.2: it was upside down and mispositioned, because the offset used (-(control_assembly_z + cage_bearing_tip_native_z), no rotation) ignored the rotate([180,0,0]) that src/Full_Turtle.scad's positioned_sail_frame() and positioned_cage_assembly() each apply when installing the cage/frame group against the fixed cap+bottle group -- a real orientation flip between bottle-native space and this module's own frame-native space, not just a Z offset. Rederived the correct transform by composing each of Full_Turtle's four placement chains (bottle/cap/cage/sail_frame, all siblings in one shared pre-outer-flip coordinate space) and inverting the frame's own chain against the other three -- verified by hand against the cage line, which reduces cleanly to this file's own existing cage_bearing_tip_native_z convention. Also, per this request: show_control_bottle now additionally draws control_cap() and control_cage() (new use <control_cap.scad> / <control_cage.scad>), not just the bottle -- control_reference_native() (renamed from control_bottle_native()) places all three: bottle + cap via translate(0,0,control_assembly_z-or-cage_bearing_tip_native_z) . rotateY(180), cage via translate(0,0,cage_bearing_tip_native_z) . rotateZ(90). Rendered part=assembly with show_control_bottle=true in OpenSCAD (two camera angles): the bottle's cut/open end now correctly meets the cap's flat face, the cage sits directly above that under the cap, and the bottle's own neck+screwcap hang below through the frame -- matching how the full turtle actually installs it (bottle mounted neck-down). No ERROR/WARNING. Separately tried reducing top_sail_bar_axle_hole_diameter 12->8 mm as requested but reverted it: build/lint.py caught a real physical conflict -- the axle's 10 mm-AF hex section is ~11.55 mm across corners (hex_corner_diameter) and must pass through this hole per the existing assert and CLAUDE.md s9's 'a 10 mm-AF hex... fitting the Ø12 sail-bar opening' -- an 8 mm hole is too small for it. Flagged to the user rather than silently keeping the old value or breaking the assert; left at 12 mm pending direction. Component-scoped to lib/sail_frame.scad (no lib/params.scad or shared-signature change), effect fully visible in OpenSCAD views -- per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5, build/test.py was neither run nor recommended.

Bottom ballast fin: bl_fin_front_chamfer() was 1.5*bl_t() (18 mm at reference params), leaving only 0.5*bl_t() (6 mm) of solid material between the chamfer and the lower slot above it (bl_fin_lower_protrusion() = 2*bl_t() = 24 mm) -- a thin sliver right where two cuts meet, the same kind of unnecessarily-weakened joint flagged on the sail frame's bottom rail in this session. Changed to bl_fin_lower_protrusion() - bl_t() (= bl_t(), 12 mm), giving a full board-thickness of solid wood between the two cuts. Position and shape of the chamfer (still the corner clip at the fin's near end) are unchanged, only its size. build/build.py + build/lint.py clean. Component-scoped to lib/ballast_fin.scad (no lib/params.scad or shared-signature change), effect fully visible in one OpenSCAD view (bl_fin_profile_2d()'s corner chamfer shrinks, the rest of the fin is untouched) -- per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5, build/test.py was neither run nor recommended. PROPAGATION (CLAUDE.md s19): this value is vendored by ../hopeTurtles.org/generator/bottom_ballast_fin_generator.py (ballast_fin_front_chamfer) and generator/objects/ballast.py (derive_dimensions()'s ballast_fin_front_chamfer) -- both updated in the same task to match (see that repo's own changelog/SYNC_LOG for the corresponding entry).

Three sail-apparatus changes, all component-scoped to lib/sail_frame.scad. (1) New show_control_bottle=false arg on sail_frame() (wired through the standalone wrapper): when true, draws lib/bottle_mockup.scad's cut_bottle() -- the bottle only, no control cap and no cage -- inside the frame's own native coordinates, positioned with the same relative offset (control_assembly_z + cage_bearing_tip_native_z) that src/Full_Turtle.scad's positioned_sail_frame() uses to place the frame against the bottle, just applied in reverse. Confirmed visually: rendered part=assembly with show_control_bottle=true, the bottle sits centred through the battens with its cut/neck end at the top, no cap/cage geometry present. (2) Confirmed (not changed) the top sail bar's axle hole: top_sail_bar_axle_hole_diameter is a hard-limited Oe12 mm round hole (lib/sail_frame.scad, top_sail_bar_profile_2d()). (3) Removed the bottom sail bar's second ('complementary half-lap') mortise cut for the joint strengthener -- the rail was carrying two interlocking slots (its own batten slot plus a full-thickness strengthener mortise) in the same cross-section, which the user identified as an avoidable weak point. The rail now keeps only its own batten slot. joint_strengthener_part()'s own notch is unchanged (its floor is the horizontal shelf the rail now simply rests on), and it gains a new vertical Oe6.4 mm (batten_cage_m6_hole_diameter) screw clearance hole straight down through the solid section above the notch to the notch floor, so the strengthener is screwed down onto the rail from above instead of interlocking with it. Removed the now-unused joint_strengthener_rail_slot_offset local. build/build.py + build/lint.py clean (0 problem groups, full OpenSCAD parse of every lib/src/bundle file including Full_Turtle_v1.scad, since sail_frame.scad is shared-contract-adjacent -- it's consumed by both the standalone wrapper and src/Full_Turtle.scad). Visual check: rendered part=assembly with and without show_control_bottle; no new ERROR/WARNING. Per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5 this stayed within one subsystem with effects fully visible in OpenSCAD views, so build/test.py was neither run nor recommended. No lib/params.scad value or module signature default changed, so no HopeTurtles.org generator propagation is needed (the sails generator's own frame formulas are unaffected -- CLAUDE.md s19).

Fixed a real assembly bug: the bottom plate's 3 alignment pegs and top plate's 3 alignment holes were both placed at the same angles (90/210/330) in each module's own as-modelled coordinates, but srm_top_plate is modelled parting-face-DOWN and only reaches its 'as used' orientation via a PHYSICAL 180-deg turn after printing (the print-time mold_top pose is a pure Z-mirror, which a real part cannot do -- turning it over is a rotation about an in-plane axis, which also negates Y). So the printed holes land at the mirrored angles (-90/-210/-330) once actually turned over to seat on the bottom plate, and the old matching-angle pegs missed them entirely -- the two halves could not register. Fixed by moving the BOTTOM plate's peg angles to -90/-210/-330 (holes stay at 90/210/330) as requested. Verified numerically (a standalone OpenSCAD echo of both peg positions and the top plate's post-flip hole positions) that all three pairs now coincide exactly: [0,-43.625], [-37.78,21.81], [37.78,21.81]. Also exposed the FLAT insert-seal ring's (the large ring, not the small nested axle O-ring) as-cast inner diameter, outer diameter and axial thickness as three literal customizer variables at the top of src/components/Silicone_Ring_Mold.scad (flat_ring_inner_d/outer_d/axial_t, defaulting to the current lib/params.scad-derived values 59.25/79.25/2.6), threaded through as new ring_inner_d/ring_outer_d/ring_axial_t args on lib/silicone_ring_mold.scad's silicone_ring_molds() (and down into srm_bottom_plate/srm_top_plate/ring_shape and their asserts) -- so the mold's cavity size can be tweaked per-export for a one-off STL without touching lib/params.scad (which also feeds the cap groove). The rim/peg/hole layout now follows ring_outer_d rather than a hardcoded function call, so an override also resizes the mold body and peg placement consistently. Verified: build/build.py + build/lint.py clean (0 problem groups); rendered part=mold_bottom with flat_ring_outer_d overridden to 90 mm in OpenSCAD -- meshed cleanly, echo confirmed the override took effect (79.25 -> 90) with no new ERROR/WARNING. Component-scoped to lib/silicone_ring_mold.scad + its wrapper (no lib/params.scad or shared-signature change) -- per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5, build/test.py was neither run nor recommended; visual/numeric inspection was sufficient. PLA/mold-only -- no HopeTurtles.org generator propagation needed (CLAUDE.md s19).

Three control-cap changes. (1) p_button_radius() 24 -> 25 mm (button centres now 50 mm apart, was 48) -- a shared value consumed by both control_cap and control_cage, so the cage's matching button bore moves with it; the cap wrapper's hole_spacing_cc literal was updated to match. (2) New tab_wire_hole feature (tab_wire_hole/tab_wire_hole_d/tab_wire_hole_exit_from_lip on control_cap(), wire_hole/wire_hole_d/wire_hole_exit_from_lip on cap_side_tabs()): a 5 mm-diameter capsule-shaped channel drilled down each side tab, from its exposed free tip (open air above the cap) down to a point inside the cap body, angled inward so it breaks through the tab's inner face into the hollow cavity -- for routing button wires. Modelled as a hull of two spheres between the entry point (tip, centred in the tip's radial thickness) and the exit point (default 15 mm below the lip, one full hole-diameter past the tab's inner face at that height, guaranteeing a clear breakthrough rather than a tangent graze). Wrapper turns it on (tab_wire_hole_enable = true) alongside the existing side tabs. (3) p_cap_boss_depth() 2 -> 1.5 mm (the centre boss 'lowered' 0.5 mm), so p_cap_bearing_len() (roof + boss) is now 6.5 mm (was 7); the wrapper's centre_boss_depth literal was updated to match. All three verified: build/lint.py clean; part="cap" rendered and meshed in OpenSCAD with no ERROR/WARNING (Simple: yes, echo confirms roof/boss/bearing = 5/1.5/6.5, button-hole assert passed at radius 25, wire-hole echo present); hand-checked the wire-hole geometry numerically against the default tab dimensions (entry r=35.5 at the tip, exit r=30.5 at 25 mm height, comfortably inside the tab's radial envelope at the tip and inside the cavity's own r_inner=35.5 at the exit). p_button_radius and p_cap_boss_depth both move mating interfaces (cage button alignment; axle bearing length), so this is a minor (+0.1.0) bump. Cross-subsystem mesh regression (build/test.py) was not run -- recommended to the maintainer per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5, not run automatically.

Migrated the Bottle_Control_Cap_v1XX.scad hand-built test variant into the master control cap. Two additions: (1) optional internal SIDE TABS (cap_side_tabs()) -- two ribs rooted at the insert cavity floor on the button axis, running the full cavity height then continuing 28 mm past the top lip as a free post with a gradual inward taper (6 mm total lean starting 10 mm below the lip), the pair rotated -12 deg off the button axis; new control_cap() params side_tabs/tab_width_p/tab_depth_p/tab_overhang_p/tab_fillet_p/tab_taper_gain_p/tab_taper_start_p/tab_rotate_p (side_tabs defaults false in the lib module, wrapper turns it on); (2) p_cap_axle_bore_d() 8.6 -> 8.7 mm (0.3 -> 0.35 mm radial clearance to the Ø8 axle). Both were explicitly flagged in the v1XX header as unvalidated fit/registration experiments; the user chose to adopt both as the new default per an explicit prompt during this task. Also fixed the wrapper's stale band_channel_w (2 -> 2.7) to match the already-current p_seal_groove_axial_h() default. The v1XX bottle-diameter override (86 mm) needed no action -- p_bottle_d() was already 86 in this working tree from prior uncommitted work. build/lint.py clean; part="cap" rendered and meshed cleanly in OpenSCAD (Simple: yes) with the expected echo values (disk/insert/height 100/83/40, bore 8.7, side-tab echo present). p_cap_axle_bore_d moves a mating interface (axle round-section fit), so this is a minor (+0.1.0) bump; cross-subsystem mesh regression (build/test.py) was not run -- recommended to the maintainer, not run automatically per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5.

changelog.note: Retuned the seal ring/groove fit from the 2.0.0 pass. p_seal_ring_axial_t() 3 -> 2.6 mm; p_seal_groove_axial_h() 3.5 -> 2.7 mm (0.1 mm ring-vs-groove margin, down from 0.5 -- a deliberately tighter fit per this request). p_seal_ring_radial_w() (10), elasticity_reduction (0.25) and all bottle/insert-diameter cascades from 2.0.0 unchanged. At current (86 mm bottle) reference params the flat ring is now AS-CAST ID/OD/axial = 59.25 / 79.25 / 2.6 mm, mating (installed) ID = 79 mm. Also updated the hand-built lib/-independent test variant v1.0 SCADs/Bottle_Control_Cap_v1XX.scad's own band_channel_w 2 -> 2.7 to match (that file carries its own inlined snapshot and does not track lib/params.scad automatically). build/build.py + build/lint.py clean; full mesh render of Silicone_Ring_Mold part="mold", Bottle_Control_Cap_v1 and Bottle_Control_Cap_v1XX all Simple: yes, no new ERROR/WARNING, no failed asserts (2.6 <= 2.7 clears the mold's ring-vs-groove sanity check). Shared-contract change per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5: build/test.py not run by the agent, recommended to the maintainer along with build/baseline.py if these bounds moves should be re-recorded. PLA/mold-only -- no HopeTurtles.org generator propagation needed (CLAUDE.md s19).

(a) BOTTLE INTERFACE BREAK: p_bottle_d() 82 -> 86 mm, every other bottle dimension (height, dome heights, cap/collar diameters, wall thickness) held. Cascades: p_insert_shaft_d() 79->83, p_seal_groove_root_d() 75->79, p_port_height() (== bottle dia, asserted) 82->86, Ecojoiner john_height/john_length/rectangle_y, top_crossbar_len 492->516, bottom_rail_len 246->258, ballast_core_w/slat_gap/slat_spacing/board_len/fin_len all grow accordingly. FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: src/Full_Turtle.scad's top-level `bottle_diameter` was a hardcoded 82 literal, NOT derived from p_bottle_d() despite the file's own comment calling that block 'SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH' -- it silently matched by coincidence until this change, at which point the rear-fin/Little-John Y-axis cross-check assert (added in 1.8.0) correctly caught the resulting drift between the full assembly's own Ecojoiner-rectangle copy (stuck on the old 82-based value) and lib-derived values (now 86-based). Now `bottle_diameter = p_bottle_d()`; assert passes, build/lint.py clean. (b) Silicone mold retune for real (stretchy) silicone: new p_seal_ring_elasticity_reduction() = 0.25 -- the cast ring's inner diameter is now 25% SMALLER than the groove root it mates to (lib/silicone_ring_mold.scad _srm_cast_inner_d()), so the ring is under radial tension once stretched onto the cap instead of a slack 1:1 as-cast fit. p_seal_ring_axial_t() 1.5->3 mm and p_seal_ring_radial_w() 5->10 mm (both doubled, per request). CONSEQUENTIAL CHANGE beyond the literal ask, flagged rather than silently skipped or silently bypassing the safety assert: doubling the ring's axial thickness to 3 mm exceeds the existing 2 mm p_seal_groove_axial_h(), which the mold's own 'cast ring must not be taller than the groove it seats in' assert correctly caught -- so p_seal_groove_axial_h() was deepened 2 -> 3.5 mm (lib/control_cap.scad's groove cut) to keep the same 0.5 mm ring-vs-groove clearance margin the reference design had. At the new 86 mm-bottle reference params the flat ring is now: AS-CAST ID/OD/axial = 59.25 / 79.25 / 3 mm, mating (installed, stretched) ID = 79 mm (the groove root). Nominal, no shrinkage compensation; the stretch-fit tension level (25%) and the retuned groove depth are NOT physically validated -- flagged in lib/silicone_ring_mold.scad and CLAUDE.md s8 as before. build/build.py + build/lint.py clean (OpenSCAD parse of every lib/src/bundle file, including a full mesh render of Silicone_Ring_Mold part="mold" and Bottle_Control_Cap_v1 -- both Simple: yes, no new ERROR/WARNING). SHARED-CONTRACT CHANGE per CLAUDE.md s15 step 5: build/test.py (full cross-subsystem mesh regression) was NOT run by the agent -- recommended to the maintainer, along with build/baseline.py for the intentional bounds moves (bottle-diameter cascade + groove/ring redimension), but not run automatically. HopeTurtles.org generator propagation (CLAUDE.md s19) also NOT done in this pass -- lib/params.scad, lib/control_cap.scad (groove) and the wooden-part formulas that scale with p_bottle_d() all need the sync/check steps in ../hopeTurtles.org/generator/; flagged as an open item pending maintainer action (silicone mold + cap/groove are PLA/mold-only and need no generator propagation, per s19's PLA-only exemption -- only the bottle-diameter cascade into the wooden-part generators is open).

Cage roof-top cleanup. (a) p_cage_roof_t() 6 -> 4 mm. Ecojoiner port length is now DERIVED: p_port_length() = p_top_dome_h() + new p_port_allowance() (62 + 20 = 82). It was the evaluated constant 82, which broke the rule for any bottle whose top taper differs from the reference bottle - the HopeTurtles.org generators already derive it as taper_height + port_allowance, and lib is the source of truth for the rule. Value unchanged at defaults, so no geometry, bounds or baseline move; every bundle regenerates because params.scad is inlined in all of them. Bridge to the generators documented in CLAUDE.md section 19.

Added a genuine cross-check assert for the rear-fin/Ecojoiner M6 mounting-hole alignment. The existing assert ("Rear-fin and John mounting-hole axes must coincide") only checked the X axis (hole_from_front) against a value DEFINED from the same terms it compares to, so it could never fail - it was not proof the shafts are actually flush against the John. Verified via rendered coordinate probes (real board geometry, not just formulas) that the current model IS already correctly aligned on the Y axis (the boards' stacking direction) - the two rear-fin shaft boards meet their target Little John boards flush, with zero gap, at Y=6 and Y=112. No placement values changed; geometry and bounds are unchanged (assert-only addition), confirmed via build/lint.py's OpenSCAD parse plus a manual numeric negative-control test showing the new assert's terms would diverge under a simulated 12mm regression.

Restored the Master John. One of the six Little Johns in the standalone Ecojoiner (eco_ecojoiner_only) is now the deeper-slotted piece fitted last: same outline, collar hole and M6 holes, but its two top slots are cut to eco_master_slot_depth() = min(floor(port_height/2), floor(john_height*0.6)) = 34 mm instead of the standard 29, so it can drop past the already-seated Johns of the almost-closed frame. Without the deeper slot the third rectangle cannot be assembled. The rule is lifted verbatim from the HopeTurtles.org 6FC generator (objects/ecojoiner_6fc.py::master_slot_depth), which had always carried it - this is a sanctioned upstream lift under CLAUDE.md s19 ('lib owns the rule'), reversing the 2026-09-08 v1.7.1 sync that had wrongly flattened it away.
